title: Adjuster Authorization Terms by Program — Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Adjuster authorization terms — Workers' Compensation Referral

The figures on this card set, program by program, how adjuster authorization works on a Workers' Compensation Referral: whether an adjuster must authorize treatment, how many visits may be given before an authorization, when a pending request is followed up, how far ahead of the end date and at what remaining balance an extension is requested, and whether a visit given without a required authorization may ever be billed to the injured worker.

| Program | Adjuster authorization required | Visits before authorization (incl. initial evaluation) | Follow-up on pending request (business days) | Extension lead time before end date (calendar days) | Extension trigger (remaining visits or program days) | Unauthorized visit billable to worker |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employer Direct Early Intervention | No | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | No |
| Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy | Yes | 1 | 3 | 5 | 2 | No |
| Workers' Comp Post-Surgical Therapy | Yes | 1 | 3 | 5 | 2 | No |
| Work Conditioning Program | Yes | 0 | 3 | 3 | 3 | No |
| Work Hardening Program | Yes | 0 | 3 | 3 | 3 | No |
| Functional Capacity Evaluation | Yes | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | No |

## What each figure means

- **Adjuster authorization required** — whether the adjuster must authorize treatment before it is rendered beyond the visits allowed before authorization.
- **Visits before authorization** — the visits, the initial evaluation counted among them, that may be rendered before an adjuster authorization.
- **Follow-up on a pending request** — the business days after an authorization request after which it is followed up with the adjuster; 0 where no authorization is needed.
- **Extension lead time** — the calendar days before the authorization end date by which an extension is requested; 0 where not applicable.
- **Extension trigger** — the remaining authorized visits or program days at or below which an extension is requested; 0 where not applicable.
- **Unauthorized visit billable to worker** — whether a visit rendered without a required authorization may be billed to the worker.

## Points of comparison

- Employer Direct Early Intervention is the only program with no adjuster authorization requirement; its follow-up, lead-time and trigger figures are all 0.
- Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy and Workers' Comp Post-Surgical Therapy each allow 1 visit before authorization; Work Conditioning Program, Work Hardening Program and Functional Capacity Evaluation allow 0.
- A pending request is followed up after 3 business days in every authorized program except Functional Capacity Evaluation, where the figure is 2.
- The two therapy programs request an extension 5 calendar days ahead of the end date or at 2 remaining visits; Work Conditioning and Work Hardening use 3 calendar days and 3 remaining program days.
- No program allows a visit given without a required authorization to be billed to the worker.
